findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment:
Observed the following time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods above the safe maximum cold holding temperature in the 2-door drawer cooler under the grill:
1. Gyro meat (60.9F with probe)
2. Two containers of raw hamburger (60.0F and 62.3F with probe
3. Sliced cheese (63.4F with probe)
4. BBQ Pork (56.8F with probe)
The PIC was informed and chose to discard all TCS foods in the cooler. The PIC investigated the cooler further and discovered that the power switch had been accidentally turned off. The cooler was turned on and reached 41F during today’s visit. Since the items were discarded and the cooler is operational, this violation is considered corrected-on-site.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: The inspector observed pests present in the kitchen, dish area, and bar spaces. The insects were observed present on glue traps in all three spaces. The PIC informed the inspector that active pest control measures are being taken. Pest control is currently visiting the facility every two weeks. The inspector recommends writing dates on all glue traps for monitoring purposes, sealing all holes and coving to prevent pest movement, and deep cleaning the floors and equipment to starve out pests. The inspector will spot check the facility to confirm pest reduction in the 30 days (2/17/2026 to avoid weekend and holiday). Ensure receipts of pest control visits are kept in the facility for the inspector to view.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment:
Observed the following time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods above the safe maximum cold holding temperature in the 2-door cooler:
1. Cottage cheese
2. Sour cream
3. Coleslaw
4. Tavern cheese
5. Cut lettuce
6. Cut tomato
7. Caesar dressing
8. Ranch dressing
9. Shredded cheese

These items all measured roughly 50-60 degrees with the infrared thermometer. The digital thermometer for the cooler read 43F. The PIC was informed and chose to discard all TCS foods in the cooler. The PIC called and scheduled maintenance on the cooler. Since the items were discarded, this violation is considered corrected-on-site.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment:
Repeat Violation

Observed RTE eat foods (sour cream, cottage cheese) to be dated according to expiration date on original packaging. Advised PIC that RTE foods transferred into new packaging must be dated to reflect 7 days following the opening of the original container. Due to the failure of the cooler, these items were voluntarily discarded. Education was conducted with the PIC regarding proper date marking procedure and a handout was provided.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. Refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: The 2-door standing cooler was observed to measure 50-60F with the infrared probe. The interior of the cooler was not cold to the touch. The PIC was informed and determined that the cooler was not operational. Maintenance on the cooler was scheduled during the inspection. A follow-up will be conducted on 6/20/2025 to ensure the cooler has been repaired. In the meantime, the 2-door standing cooler cannot be used to store TCS foods. The walk-in will be used until the service is completed.

3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114.

Observed single-use utensils to be stored in metal tubs which were contaminated with dust and food debris. Observed single-use condiment cups to be stored with food contact surfaces exposed or without adequate coverings to protect from dust/debris contamination. Observed large sharpies to be in a container with plastic spoons. Advised PIC to keep containers holding single-use utensils clean and to keep single-use food contact surfaces covered or inverted on a clean surface such as the bottom of a container or clean work surface. Containers holding single-use utensils were washed and contaminated utensils were disposed of during inspection.

(C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-302.14: There were no chlorine test strips available during the inspection. The facility had pH test strips. Provide chlorine test strips to ensure sanitizer solutions are at proper concentrations. Test strips provided by the inspector. The proper type of test strips were discussed with the manager. 
A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: Observed the hood baffles to have an accumulation of grease. Also, the walk in cooler (WIC) fan was dusty. Ensure these surfaces are cleaned more frequently so they are maintained clean. 
 NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: Observed the floor under the fryers and flat top grill to be heavily soiled with food, grease, and other debris. Ensure these surfaces are cleaned frequently so they are maintained clean. 
(A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Observed the kitchen sani bucket to be at a concentration of 0ppm of bleach. Sani buckets must maintain a concentration between 50ppm and 200ppm of bleach. The sani bucket was remade during the inspection. 
Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text: 750.540 (C) The food establishment is not under the operational supervision of a Certified Food Service Sanitation Manager that is present at appropriate times. Provide an adequate number of staff with approved training. Reference 750.540. Certified manager arrived after I arrived. Schedule and keep certified manager on duty at all times food is prepared and sold.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B)  (P) Foods in the drawers of the low boy are between 44°F and 56°F. Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 41°F, or less. Reviewed cold holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequately held food was discarded. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B). Facility voluntarily discarded 4 lbs of bbq pork at 51°F , 3 lbs of brisket at 50°F, 2 lbs of gyro meat at 50°F , 13lbs of 5 oz burger portions at 47°F .  Olives and other items in the top drawer were discarded.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17  (Pf) Milk and OJ in the bar cooler of the facility are not marked with a use-by date.  Foods were marked. Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours must be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food must be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 41°F or less for a maximum of 7 days. Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17. Ensure that all items are properly date marked.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12  (C) In-Use Utensils are stored incorrectly at the ice scoop. Observed the ice scoop holder at the bar to have water in the bottom. The scoop and holder were removed and sanitized. Store in-use utensils: 1) in the food with the handle above the top of the food item; 2) on a clean and sanitized surface; 3) in running water; 4) in a container of hot water maintained at or above 135 °F. Reference 3-304.12.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Soil residue present on the soda gun at the bar and the inside of the hot holding unit. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13. Clean and maintain free of accumulated soil.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 (A & B) (C) The floor to the right of the fryers behind and under the pipe on the ground are soiled. Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. Except for cleaning up a spill or other accident, cleaning should be done during periods when the least amount of food is exposed such as after closing.  Reference 6-501.12 (A & B).

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.citation_text: 2-401.11  (C) Employee observed drinking from an uncovered cup in the food preparation areas. Provide a lid and straw for beverage cups. Store personal drinks in an area where they will not potentially contaminate food or single service items.  Reference 2-401.11. Cups were removed.

Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 41°F, or less. Reviewed cold holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequately held food was discarded. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B).

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment: Observed a box of napkins on the floor in the dry storage area. Store single use items properly.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(A) and (C)  (C) Single-Use Articles are stored incorrectly. Single-Use Articles shall be stored: 1) in a clean and dry location; 2) away or protected from contamination; 3) at least six inches above the floor; 4) covered or inverted. Reference 4-903.11(A) and (C).

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.citation_text: 3-501.14  (P) Chili put to cool at 11am is 107°F. Food did not cool from 135°F to 70°F within two hours and from 135°F to 41°F or less within a total of 6 hours. Reviewed cooling requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequately cooled food was discarded. Reference 3-501.14.  Three half pans of chili between 107 and 114F were discarded in the garbage. No time or temp on the itmes. No cooling temperature logs kept. Use active methods to properly cool chili in the future.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2)  (P) Hamburger in the low boy is observed to be 54F. Gyro meat is observed to be held at 56F. Impossible burgers observed to be 56F. Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 41°F, or less. Reviewed cold holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadaquiately held food was voluintarily discarded. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2). 28 big burgers, 5 reguarl sized burgers, 7 impossible burgers and approximately 3 pounds of gyro meat were discarded. Technician was called to repair the low boy. Do not use this unit for TCS foods until it is repaired.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17  (Pf) Date of 4/30 marked on chili on hot holding unit exceeds the time limit. Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours must be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food must be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 41°F or less for a maximum of 7 days. Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.citation_text: 3-501.15  (Pf) The method of cooling chili is inadequate. Use one or more of the following methods based on the type of food being cooled: placing the food in shallow pans; separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; using containers that facilitate heat transfer; adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Discussed HACCP concept with the person in charge. Reference 3-501.15. Keep cooling logs and or place temperature date and time on the food so that time in the temperature danger zone can be adequately evaluated. Food was discarded.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14  (C) In-use wiping cloths are observed to be stored in sanitizer that is not proper strenght. Cloths used for wiping spills shall be maintained dry. Cloths used to wipe surfaces and equipment shall be held in proper sanitizer solution. Cloths in-use for wiping surfaces in contact with raw animalfoods shall be kept separate from cloths used for other purposes. In-use cloths must be laundered daily. Reference 3-304.14. Sanitizer bucket was remade to have proper chlorine sanitizer concentration.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.citation_text: 4-901.11  (C) Equipment/Utensils are not properly Air-Dried after cleaning and sanitizing at the wait service area. After cleaning and sanitizing all equipment and utensils shall be air dried before use. Reference 4-901.11.
